editorial:
Imagine sitting in a lonely spot with nothing to do but talk to your best friend while you wait for someone who might never show up. That is exactly what you get with this Swedish take on the famous play. You follow two guys, Vladimir and Estragon, who spend their entire day chatting, arguing, and wondering about a man named Godot. The vibe is very strange and a bit sad, but it also feels like a weird comedy because the characters say such odd things to each other. It feels less like a movie and more like you are eavesdropping on a private conversation between two lost souls.

What really works here is the acting, as the leads make the boredom feel real without being dull. The pacing is slow on purpose, so you have to be in the right mood for it. If you enjoy stories that make you think about life and time, you will love this. It is a great piece of art to experience if you have a quiet evening. You can find this via streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, or you might want to rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. If you are a film buff, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: At the end, a boy arrives to tell the two men that Godot is not coming today but will surely come tomorrow. The men feel let down and tired. They talk about leaving the spot and going home, but the movie ends with a twist: they say they are leaving, but they do not actually move. They just stay standing there, stuck in their endless loop of waiting.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about the meaning of life and strange conversations.
